title: Synthetic SLAM Journal
heading: From six seconds of generated video to a 3D map, one stage at a time
eyebrow: Engineering journal · October 8, 2026 · AMB3R-SLAM · Depth Anything 3 · Seedance 2.5 · RTX 4090
lede: A text prompt became a 6 s video of a small robot rolling through a junkyard. AMB3R-SLAM turned its 145 frames, plain RGB from one uncalibrated camera, into a camera path and a 3.33 million-point coloured map in 19.9 s on one GPU. We opened the pipeline into eight stages, recorded what each one produced, and built a viewer that replays them all in 3D.
description: A generated junkyard video, run through AMB3R-SLAM stage by stage: front-end tracking, feed-forward submaps, Sim(3) stitching, long-context links, loop retrieval, pose graph and map, with a 3D replay viewer.

hero.caption: The SLAM camera (yellow frustum, showing the frame it sees) and its path (orange) as the map grows, with the generated input video in the corner, at 1×; then an orbit of the finished map. Rendered on the CPU from the recorded run; each point appears when the camera passes the frame it came from.

scope: What this is. The video is generated from a text prompt by Seedance 2.5; no robot or camera recorded it. AMB3R-SLAM (Wang and Agapito, 2026) runs unmodified from a pinned submodule; our tracer wraps its methods at run time to keep every intermediate result. The images, figures, film and viewer all come from one recorded run; every number on this page is in docs/synthetic_slam/results/. Distances are in the model's own units: one camera cannot measure absolute scale.
footer: Source, documentation and recorded results: rozgo/world-sandbox, docs/synthetic_slam/. SLAM: AMB3R-SLAM by Hengyi Wang and Lourdes Agapito (arXiv 2609.19518, Apache 2.0), pinned at commit 5418465. Models: Depth Anything 3, DA3-Small (Apache 2.0) and DA3-Nested-Giant-Large-1.1 (CC BY-NC 4.0). Loop retrieval: DBoW2 with the ORB-SLAM3 vocabulary; covisibility: ALIKED; each under its own licence in the submodule's thirdparty/. Video: ByteDance Seedance 2.5 text-to-video through WaveSpeed. Viewer: three.js r170 (MIT). This is an independent illustration, not a result of those authors.

card.line: Six seconds of generated robot video become a camera path and a 3.33 M-point map in 19.9 s, with every stage of AMB3R-SLAM opened up and replayable in 3D.
